pre_schema_admission_ownership_rulings.ruling: The family defines an owner-namespaced stream and typed event projection. It mints no sequence, admission decision, receipt, state root, receipt root, or transition chain; append order, expected-head conflict handling, accepted roots, and receipts are referenced from the canonical Agentgres operation.

The family defines subscriber scope, filters, expiry/revocation, backpressure policy, and an acknowledged-checkpoint projection. It mints no admission or checkpoint receipt and owns no transition chain; every lease transition and checkpoint advance references the canonical Agentgres operation and receipt.

Typing and event classes: event kinds are typed by owner-declared payload schema refs scoped to the stream owner namespace; the family defines no closed global event-kind enum and admits no consumer vocabulary — including M5.0 GoalRun/thread-orchestration fields — as an admission-required field. Each owner namespace declares its admitted-truth classes versus ephemeral delivery-only classes; the numeric interactive latency budget for the ephemeral path is owned by the canon pass recorded in stages/m5.md canon gaps, not by this record.

adversarial_or_fault_proof: Unleased delivery, cross-owner filters, expired/revoked leases, lag, checkpoint substitution, dropped adapter frames, restart, and rebase ambiguity fail closed or emit typed outcomes.

An ephemeral-class event presented for truth admission and an admitted-class event delivered without admission both fail closed with typed outcomes; any consumer-vocabulary field required at admission is a contract defect.

current_implementation_evidence: ADR 0030 TEST FINDING (measured 2026-08-01, branch agent/hypervisor-m4-end-state @219154326): the interim runtime thread-event plane this successor replaces is a parallel admission spine at the thread layer. crates/services/src/agentic/runtime/kernel/runtime_thread_event.rs mints its own per-stream admission sequence (seq = latest_seq + 1 read back from <state_dir>/events/<sha256(stream)>.jsonl), its own state-root chain (state_root_before/state_root_after), resulting heads, and admission decisions (status "admitted" plus admission_hash); its storage admission (AgentgresAdmissionCore.admit_storage_backend_write) validates shape and mints a local hash. Canonical Agentgres (crates/agentgres mux — the substrate M4 room transitions admit through in outcome_room_system_routes.rs) is never in the path; concurrency is the per-stream file lock event_log_bridge::with_event_stream_lock, not expected-head CAS (direct admission rejects caller-supplied expected_head/latest_seq/state_root_before, so no CAS refusal semantics exist); minted refs wear the fabricated namespace agentgres://runtime-events/... implying canonical admission that never happened. runtime_thread_fork_control.rs and runtime_managed_session_control.rs plan events admitted through that same path (daemon admit_and_persist_event) and mint receipt-ref identities (receipt_thread_fork_control_{fork_hash}, receipt_runtime_managed_session_projection_*) that no canonical receipt object backs — fabricated to satisfy the admission's MissingReceiptRefs floor. CONSEQUENCE: naive descriptive contracts for runtime-thread-event / thread-fork-control / managed-session-control would register this second spine's owned sequence/root/head/hash fields, which ADR 0030 forbids; the registered siblings (harness-session-binding-admission.v1, hypervisor-session-launch-recipe-admission.v1) show the allowed shape — agentgres_operation_refs/receipt_refs/state_root as references only, no owned chain. DISPOSITION: filed, not executed (post-ADR-0031 correction boundary). Contract paths: (a) after this successor re-homes accepted events onto atomic Agentgres head/root transitions, describe the re-homed admission; or (b) sibling-style request/decision reference contracts owning no sequence/root/chain field. The choice is an owner decision at M5.0 shaping. CRATE-BOUNDARY FORK AND RULING (2026-08-02). Measured while re-homing: of the three writers on the per-stream lock, two are daemon-side (lifecycle_routes.rs:948 admit_and_persist_event, :986 persist_thread_events) but the third is event_log_bridge.rs:294 in crates/services (ioi-services), which has NO agentgres dependency, while the admission core sits in crates/node/src/bin/hypervisor_daemon_routes/substrate_store.rs — a BINARY module the services crate structurally cannot call. Three options were surfaced; the implementer took no default. OPTION 3 (re-home the two daemon writers, file the bridge as residue) was REJECTED on the implementer's own analysis and the owner's concurrence: one writer appending kernel-minted seq while two admit through Agentgres gives a SINGLE STREAM two sequence authorities, violating the per-stream atomicity constraint and reproducing the decay-into-dual-read path with extra steps. OPTION 2 (bridge calls the daemon's HTTP route) was REJECTED as worse than first framed: ioi-node links ioi-services, so the bridge runs INSIDE the daemon process — the call is a loopback self-call into the daemon's own listener, carrying re-entrancy, middleware re-entry, and deadlock surface, plus contexts where the listener is not up. OWNER RULING — OPTION 1: lift the admission core into crates/agentgres (not a new crate: refs.rs already established that backed constructors live there, and ADR 0003 makes Agentgres operation/head/root/receipt the domain truth, so the minting discipline arguably always belonged in that crate, with the daemon remaining the canonical endpoint per ADR 0002). services -> agentgres is a clean forward DAG edge; agentgres depends on neither services nor node, so no cycle. Four binding constraints: (1) MOVE, NOT COPY — the binary-module implementation is deleted in the same change, because two admission cores is the shared-$def drift class at the code layer, with one edited and one copied and no bar firing; (2) LIFT THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE — canonicality gates, durability confirmation, and the ack-versus-projection cross-check move together, since 'admitted means admitted' is the property being lifted and splitting it across the boundary recreates the wiring-failure class; the axum/route surface stays in the daemon; (3) the same-key-different-bytes refusal moves to the library layer, which makes its negative fixture testable without a daemon boot; (4) nothing lands ahead of the M4 98/98 + 44/44 re-run at the new HEAD, since the dependency-graph change touches verified code. SIZING MEASURED FOR THE LIFT: the admission function's daemon-side dependencies are with_current_handle (a process-scoped OnceLock<Mutex<..>> handle cache over MuxHandle, plus lock_expected_absent_writer and log_generation) and confirm_required_admission_durability (engine_dir + muxlog.bin/dir sync_all). The handle cache is daemon LIFECYCLE state, not admission discipline, and stays; the lifted core takes a &MuxHandle from its caller. Durability confirmation moves with the core because agentgres owns its own on-disk layout. MuxEngine, MuxAdmitError, ExactProjection, Operation, AdmitAck and Refusal are already agentgres vocabulary, so the core's only non-agentgres imports are axum/serde/sha2/std and the axum surface is route-layer, not admission-layer. HANDLE-STEWARDSHIP WIRING, decided before the lift so nothing is improvised mid-move (owner rider 2026-08-02). Call-graph fact: lock_expected_absent_writer is taken INSIDE with_current_handle (substrate_store.rs:1955), guarding the handle-acquisition and log_generation staleness window — an flock on the engine dir, i.e. cross-process writer stewardship. Lock, generation check, and the OnceLock cache are ONE mechanism, and that mechanism is process lifecycle, not admission discipline. The flock conflicts per open-file-description, so a second in-process acquisition would not merely violate the design — it would block or fail at runtime. The invariant is therefore made STRUCTURAL rather than conventional, in the same style as the event-class control flow: (i) THE LIFTED CORE EXPOSES NO HANDLE-ACQUISITION PATH AT ALL. It accepts a &MuxHandle and cannot obtain one, so 'exactly one handle steward per process' is a fact about the library's API surface rather than a rule someone must remember. (ii) THE DAEMON INJECTS ADMISSION CAPABILITY INTO SERVICES AT BOOT. Chosen shape: a TRAIT object, not a closure — the capability already needs more than one operation (admit and read-head) and will grow lease-transition and checkpoint-advance operations, which a closure degrades into a struct-of-closures with no shared name; a trait also names the capability in refusals and makes a test double straightforward. The trait and its types live in agentgres; ioi-services gains the agentgres dependency for the TYPES ONLY (Operation, Refusal, ExactProjection) and redefines nothing, because redefinition is the shared-$def drift class at the code layer. The daemon-side implementation wraps with_current_handle around the lifted core, so the daemon keeps sole handle stewardship and the library keeps sole discipline. (iii) THE INJECTION BOUNDARY FAILS CLOSED. If the capability is absent, the bridge REFUSES with a typed refusal; it never falls back to the legacy JSONL path. This is the refusal-not-fallback constraint applied at the wiring boundary, and it is what stops an un-injected build from silently reverting to the old spine. The test-forced durability-failure hook (IOI_TEST_FORCE_REQUIRED_ADMISSION_SYNC_FAILURE) moves with the core: that fault-injection point is part of the discipline's proof surface, not daemon scaffolding. TWO ADDITIONS TO THE WIRING (owner, 2026-08-02). (iv) THE TRAIT IS A CAPABILITY SURFACE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. It stays bounded at the four named operations — admit, read-head, lease-transition, checkpoint-advance — because each method is an API decision about what the bridge is PERMITTED to do. A fifth operation requires a record arguing for it, not a commit adding it. (v) THE FAIL-CLOSED BOUNDARY NEEDS A REAL-BOOT-PATH TEST, and this follows from this record's own taxonomy rather than from caution: an un-injected build reverting to the JSONL spine is a WIRING failure, and fixtures structurally cannot reach wiring because the fixture author supplies the input set. A test that calls the refusal directly proves only the predicate. The negative set must therefore construct services state WITHOUT the capability, drive a real bridge write through it, and assert the typed refusal surfaces — sitting beside the same-key-different-bytes fixture. Absent that, the fail-closed boundary is itself a bar nobody has watched fire, which is the exact pattern this cut exists to retire. The trait's test double additionally lets the genericity verifier drive BOTH owner namespaces through the bridge path without a daemon boot, so the >= 2-namespace proof does not depend on a live plane for its bridge leg. ENTRY-POINT CONSTRAINT ON THE BOUNDARY TEST (owner refinement, 2026-08-02). "Drives a real bridge write" means the test calls the PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT — the same function the runtime calls — and not a pipeline reconstructed inside the test. A reconstructed pipeline is fixture-shape one level up: it re-supplies the call path the same way a fixture re-supplies the input set, so it would keep passing while production routed around the capability entirely. Only entry through the real function makes a vanished injection fail loudly. CONSTRAINT COLLISION FOUND DURING THE LIFT (implementer, 2026-08-02) — QUEUED, NOT DECIDED. Full-stream idempotency and the four-operation capability bound are in direct conflict for the RUNTIME-SIDE writer only. Three legs, each measured rather than reasoned: (1) the pre-existing dedup scans the WHOLE stream — lifecycle_routes.rs `for line in contents.lines()` returns the first idempotency_key match anywhere in history, and its own comment names non-consecutive duplicate sources (a re-applied restore with the same outcome); (2) `read_head` cannot serve that — `project_exact` is latest-per-object-key, so a re-homed writer sees only the newest operation; (3) the engine does NOT dedupe on idem_key natively — `Operation.idem_key` is carried through crates/agentgres/src/mux.rs but never compared. The two DAEMON writers are unaffected: they hold the handle and read history directly via `read_event_stream_history`, which is deliberately a library function and NOT a trait method — an in-process reader needs no cross-boundary permission. Only the runtime-side writer (`event_log_bridge::admit_and_persist_runtime_event`, callers at :333 managed-session snapshot and :352 thread-event json) crosses the injection boundary, where the capability is bounded at four. THREE RESOLUTIONS, ALL OWNER-SCOPE. (a) A fifth capability operation `read_history` — the ruling requires a filed record arguing for it, and this is that argument. (b) Keep four and accept head-only dedup at the runtime boundary — this NARROWS a load-bearing property and was not taken silently. (c) Route runtime-side writes through the daemon's admission route so exactly one writer has history access — architecturally strongest since it collapses three writers to one, but it changes process topology and is far beyond a reversible in-scope default. A fourth shape was evaluated and rejected as not free: keying each event by its idem_key with expected_absent makes the ENGINE enforce idempotency without any history read, but it trades away the expected-head CAS that is this cut's stated point. RULING ON THE COLLISION (owner, 2026-08-02): ALL THREE FILED OPTIONS REJECTED; key-dedup folds into admit itself. (a) rejected — read_history is the wrong grant: it exports the scan to callers and installs dedup at N call sites, the drift class one layer up. The bridge does not need 'read the stream'; it needs 'this key admits exactly once,' which is admission discipline, not a capability. (b) rejected on the implementer's own analysis — silently narrowing a load-bearing property. (c) rejected — it resurrects the loopback shape already rejected at the crate fork, and a topology change is not this cut. The fourth-shape rejection STANDS as provenance: expected-head CAS remains the spine, the chain and CAS are untouched, and key-uniqueness became a check inside the existing admission cycle. The refusal vocabulary was WIRED, not redrafted: SameKeyDifferentBytes already existed in the lifted discipline; only its enforcement scope was wrong. IMPLEMENTED. Whole-stream key enforcement now runs inside admit_event_stream_operation against the log the handle serves — never a caller-side file. Byte-identical duplicate anywhere in the stream returns the ORIGINAL exact projection with replayed=true; same key with different bytes takes the existing refusal. The four-operation surface stands; no fifth operation was added. The public library history read added at d2469eb35 was DELETED in the same change, having no non-dedup consumer — an unowned read surface is not left standing. WHY DEDUP-INSIDE-ADMIT NEEDS NO SERIALIZATION WINDOW: race safety comes from the CAS, not a lock. At most one of two concurrent same-key admits wins the expected-head compare-and-swap. The loser takes ExpectedHeadConflict, re-reads, and re-derives — and the re-derive re-runs the key scan, which now sees the winner's key and replays it. The head chain already provides the window. ONE IDENTITY DECISION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS A DEVIATION: two submissions name the same logical event by object key, operation kind, payload, and idempotency key — EXCLUDING expected_head / expected_absent and recorded_at_ms. This is not a relaxation but the correction that makes whole-stream dedup work: a duplicate arriving N events later necessarily reads a different current head and submits a different expected head, so comparing that precondition would turn every real duplicate into a same-key-different-bytes refusal. It also shows the pre-lift full-Operation comparison only ever matched a VERBATIM request replay, never the same logical event resubmitted later — which is precisely the case the caller-side scans existed to catch.
